ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law No. 80 of 2002 on Combating Money Laundering, as amended, including Law No. 36 of 2014 and subsequent amendments; Executive Regulations issued by Prime Ministerial Decree No. 951 of 2003, as amended; Law No. 8 of 2022 on the Organization and Development of the Use of Non-Cash Payment Methods; Companies Law No. 159 of 1981 and its Executive Regulations issued by Ministerial Decree No. 96 of 1982, as amended; Commercial Register Law No. 34 of 1976, as amended; Central Bank and Banking System Law No. 194 of 2020; Financial Regulatory Authority Law No. 10 of 2009, as amended. Egypt requires covered entities to identify, verify and retain information on the beneficial owner, but, as of this assessment, does not operate a generally public central UBO register equivalent to the United Kingdom register.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Before incorporation and onboarding, screen all shareholders, directors, managers, authorized signatories, UBOs, intermediaries and key suppliers against United Nations Security Council sanctions, United States OFAC lists, European Union and United Kingdom sanctions where relevant, Egyptian domestic sanctions and terrorism lists, and reputable PEP and adverse-media databases. Apply enhanced due diligence to domestic and foreign PEPs, close associates, family members, state-owned-enterprise connections, high-risk jurisdictions, nominee arrangements, unexplained wealth, cash-intensive activity and sanctioned technology or dual-use goods. Resolve false positives using documentary identifiers, retain screening evidence, prohibit anonymous ownership, and file suspicious transaction reports with the Egyptian Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing Combating Unit where legally required.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) e-Services Portal, accessible through the official GAFI investment services platform at investment.gov.eg
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The company name must be distinguishable from existing registered names, must not mislead the public regarding the company's activities or status, and must comply with Companies Law No. 159 of 1981, its Executive Regulations and GAFI filing practice. Arabic is generally required for the official corporate name and constitutional documents; a foreign-language or Latin transliteration may be used as an additional trading presentation if accepted by GAFI. A translated name does not eliminate the Arabic name requirement. The name must be consistent across the name certificate, articles of association, tax registration, commercial register, bank records and licenses.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Any name suggesting governmental sponsorship, regulated financial activity, a public authority, a protected institution or an existing famous trademark
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Obtain the GAFI name certificate before signing the final constitutional documents. File the incorporation application within the certificate's stated validity period, normally 30 days unless the issued certificate states otherwise. If rejected, obtain the written or electronic rejection reason, verify similarity, prohibited wording, Arabic-language and activity issues, and submit corrected alternative names through GAFI. Where the applicant contests the decision, file a documented grievance with the competent GAFI service office or Investment Services Center, request administrative review and preserve the filing receipt. If the administrative grievance is unsuccessful, pursue the available challenge before the competent administrative court under Egyptian State Council procedures. A rejection normally does not create a statutory right to use the rejected name while the challenge is pending.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A registered office and evidenced Egyptian address are required for company, tax and commercial-register purposes. A serviced or virtual office may be accepted for registration if supported by a valid lease, ownership document, landlord authorization and premises evidence acceptable to GAFI, the tax authority and the commercial registry. It is not a substitute for operational premises where the business stores, imports, demonstrates, repairs or distributes IoT hardware. Retailing smart-home devices may require an inventory, fulfillment, customer-service or warehouse location and may trigger import, product conformity, telecommunications, consumer-protection, e-commerce and customs requirements even where no sector-specific incorporation license is required. A purely nominal address creates material tax, banking and AML risk.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Estimated 10%-20% annual likelihood for an ordinary low-risk LLC during the initial compliance cycle, increasing materially where the registered address is shared or virtual, tax filings are late, turnover is inconsistent with declared activity, imports are material, the company seeks VAT registration, complaints are received, or AML and sanctions indicators arise. This is a risk estimate rather than a statutory probability; Egyptian authorities may conduct unannounced inspections whenever legally authorized.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Egyptian Companies Law No. 4 of 2025 (issued 5 January 2025, effective 8 July 2025, repealing Law No. 159 of 1981); Limited Liability Company formation and governance provisions applicable to LLCs; read with Investment Law No. 72 of 2017 and its executive regulations, Law No. 194 of 2020 (Commercial Registration) and relevant ministerial decrees on e-filing of incorporation contracts.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) - Companies Registration Department / One-Stop Shop (OSS), Arab Republic of Egypt
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Certificate of Incorporation issued upon registration of the Notarized Incorporation Contract (Arabic: عقد تأسيس الشركة ذات المسؤولية المحدودة) in the electronic GAFI Companies Registry
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Law No. 4 of 2025 removes any fixed minimum paid-up capital for LLCs; founders freely determine the capital in the incorporation contract and must fully subscribe it at formation. Cash quotas may be paid within five years (or a longer period stated in the contract); no escrow-bank lock-in or capital-deposit certificate is required for LLCs. In-kind quotas require a fair-valuation statement by an accredited expert.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: The sole founder and shareholder of [●] IoT Retail LLC hereby resolves: 1. Share Subscription: The subscribed capital of EGP [●], in [●] equal quotas, is ratified; each founder's subscription is accepted and credited. 2. Registered Office: The registered office is fixed at [●], [●] Governorate, Egypt, as the legal domicile for GAFI, commercial-registry, and service-of-process purposes. 3. Officers: [Name] is appointed General Manager and sole legal representative; [Name] is appointed Company Secretary/Financial Officer, each serving until removed by later resolution. All officers are authorized to complete incorporation, licensing, bank, tax, and e-invoicing filings.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log in to the GAFI OSS portal, complete the company-name search form with four alternative Arabic/Latin names for the LLC, and attach the founders' identification. The GAFI Name Screening Committee checks identical or similar registered names and trademark collisions. Once cleared, download the Name Reservation Certificate; the reservation is valid for sixty days.
required_dossiers: Name reservation application form listing four alternative names
Copy of valid passport or National ID for each founder
Power of attorney if filed through a formation agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed name is rejected for similarity, re-file with alternative names or file a written objection to the GAFI Legal Affairs Department within ten working days; resubmission is cleared same-day when no conflicting mark remains.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Justice - Notary Public Office (El-Shahar El-Aqary) with territorial jurisdiction over the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the GAFI-aligned Arabic draft incorporation contract to the notary. All founders must appear personally before the notary to confirm legal capacity and sign each page, or validly delegate under a power of attorney, which for foreign founders must be apostilled or consular-legalized. The notary stamps, authenticates, and returns the tawthiq certificate. Pay notarial fees and stamp duties at the treasury window.
required_dossiers: Incorporation contract draft in Arabic signed by all founders
Name Reservation Certificate
Passports or national IDs of all founders
Apostilled or consular-legalized power of attorney for absent or foreign founders
Receipt of stamp-duty payment
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Notarial rejection on grounds of defective signatures or unmet legal-capacity evidence is cured by correcting the contract schedule and re-attending; if foreign powers of attorney lack consular legalization, complete legalization at the Egyptian consulate of origin and resubmit.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: GAFI Registration and Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI Companies Registration Department / One-Stop Shop (OSS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit, in person or electronically, the notarized contract with the supporting dossier to the OSS. GAFI legal reviewers perform the statutory compliance check on the object clause, capital, managers, and registered address; official fees are paid through the OSS treasury. Upon clearance, the company is entered in the electronic registry and the Certificate of Incorporation (شهادة التأسيس) is issued, bearing a unique company registration number.
required_dossiers: Original notarized incorporation contract
Name Reservation Certificate
Lease contract or title deed of the registered office; written landlord no-objection
Written acceptance of office by the appointed General Manager
Authorization letter in favor of the formation counsel
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If GAFI issues a request for comments or amendment (e.g., overbroad object clause or in-kind capital valuation), respond in writing within fifteen working days. If rejected, activate the administrative appeal before the GAFI Complaint Committee and request expedition through the Investor Grievance mechanism.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Commercial Registration and Tax Card Issuance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Internal Trade - Commercial Registry Office; Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the LLC at the Commercial Registry using the GAFI certificate to obtain the Commercial Registration Certificate. Upon such registration, the ETA is notified automatically; apply for the Tax Card (البطاقة الضريبية), income-tax registration under Law No. 91 of 2005, and VAT registration at the standard rate of 14% if taxable supplies exceed the mandatory registration threshold of EGP 500,000 annually. Register for the ETA e-invoicing system because the business sells via online payment rails.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation issued by GAFI
Notarized incorporation contract copy
Commercial Registry application form
Valid lease contract of the registered office
Manager's national ID and official non-conviction / court-name clearance letter for the tax file
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Commercial Registry queries the economic activity code, submit an amended activity description aligned with ISIC 4791 (online retail of smart IoT devices). If the tax office delays the Tax Card, escalate to the ETA One-Stop Tax Window and, failing that, request GAFI inter-agency facilitation under the Investment Law.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication, Corporate Seal, Bank Account and Ancillary Post-Formation Filings
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI Publication Office / Official Gazette (Al-Waqa'i Al-Misriya); Central Bank of Egypt-licensed commercial bank; National Social Insurance Authority; ETA E-invoicing System
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: GAFI transmits the incorporation summary to the Official Gazette for publication. The Company then manufactures its corporate seal, opens a current account at a CBE-licensed bank on a certified board resolution, registers employees on the National Social Insurance e-system, and completes ETA e-invoicing registration (JSON code issuance) to reconcile Stripe and Shopify Payments flows.
required_dossiers: GAFI incorporation certificate and notarized contract
Commercial registration certificate and tax card
Certified manager resolution and full KYC documentation for bank account opening
Social insurance registration forms and employee list if hiring
ETA e-invoicing registration request and test-environment credentials
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If Gazette publication is delayed, obtain a GAFI expedition letter; if a bank refuses account opening on documentary grounds, re-present the file at another CBE-licensed bank within the free banking choice rule; if e-invoicing credentials are delayed, file a readjustment request in the ETA portal.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Industrial Development Authority (IDA) - not applicable; IDA jurisdiction under Law No. 20 of 2020 (Industrial Licensing Law) attaches only where the LLC later adds local assembly or manufacturing of IoT hardware. The current activity, online retail of smart-home IoT devices (ISIC 4791), does not trigger an industrial operating license.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: None required at formation for the current scope; a municipal commercial license (رخصة مزاولة النشاط التجاري) issued by the Local Administration Unit is mandated only if the LLC opens a physical showroom or own warehouse. Use of third-party e-commerce logistics does not trigger licensing.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Egyptian Environmental Affairs Agency (EEAA) - Ministry of Environment
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category C / Exempt: retail and warehousing of finished consumer electronics do not require a full EIA report; a self-declaration environmental commitment letter (إقرار بيئي) suffices for leased warehouse space, with Form B screening applicable only upon conversion to assembly or production.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Zero process wastewater or stack emissions; compliance is limited to municipal sanitary-sewer discharge thresholds under Ministerial Decree No. 92 of 2013 where applicable, and separate collection and delivery of end-of-life lithium batteries and electronic waste from customer returns to EEAA-licensed recyclers under hazardous-waste management rules of Law No. 4 of 1994, as amended by Law No. 9 of 2009.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Civil Defense Administration (الدفاع المدني) fire-safety and initial electrical-inspection certificates for any physical storage or showroom premises; Ministry of Manpower occupational-safety and health clearance under Law No. 12 of 2003; Social Insurance Form 1 registration for all staff.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA), e-Tax Portal at www.eta.gov.eg / tax.gov.eg
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign entities may obtain a Tax Identification Number (TIN) by submitting incorporation documents, board resolution, passport copies of managers, and local tax registration forms to the ETA; registration must be completed within 30 days of commencing activity or before first import/export customs clearance. For VAT purposes, the entity must separately register for VAT through the ETA VAT registration module.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box election exists under Egyptian tax law; LLCs are automatically subject to corporate income tax at entity level. Hybrid mismatch elections are not statutory; limited to treaty-based residency certificate elections and application of transfer pricing documentation rules.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EGP 500,000 annual taxable turnover; mandatory registration for foreign-service providers occurs upon first taxable transaction in Egypt
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory e-invoicing and e-receipt clearance through the ETA's integrated e-invoicing platform. Taxpayers must transmit invoice data in real time via APIs, receive a digital validation code, and print QR-stamped invoices for B2B and B2C transactions; non-compliance results in blocked invoices and penalties.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods exported outside Egypt qualify for 0% VAT provided physical export occurs within the statutory timeframe, an export customs declaration is registered, and the exporter retains proof of departure, sale, and foreign currency remittance. Offshore services supplied to non-residents outside Egypt may qualify if the benefit is consumed abroad and no Egyptian nexus exists.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration, Bill of Lading, Inward Remittance Certificate
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: False or overstated export zero-rating claims trigger disallowance of input VAT credits, retrospective VAT clawback, fines up to 200% of evaded tax, criminal penalties for deliberate tax evasion, and possible suspension of the taxpayer's export or VAT registrations.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Egypt (CBE) - Foreign Exchange Operations Department and the Exchange Control Administration, acting pursuant to Law No. 194 of 2020 (Central Bank and Banking System Law) and CBE Foreign Exchange Regulation No. 847 of 2020, as amended
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Egypt operates a managed-float exchange-rate regime with the EGP anchored against a U.S. dollar basket. Current-account transactions are fully convertible through licensed banks upon production of supporting commercial documentation; capital-account transactions, including inbound equity injections, shareholder loans, and profit remittances, require CBE authorization or must be effected through a CBE-authorized licensed bank under the applicable purpose-code framework. Profit and dividend remittances to non-resident shareholders are permitted but are subject to documentary hurdles: audited financial statements, Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) tax clearance, CBE Form No. 16 profit-repatriation declaration, and confirmation that the underlying profits were produced from onshore operations and have been fully disclosed in prior CBE residence filings. There are no statutory surtaxes or sequential conversion queues for genuine commercial remittances, but in periods of FX liquidity tension, banks apply an internal prioritization order favouring trade-related payments, which increases the tactical importance of maintaining a committed FX facility at a Tier-1 bank.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under CBE Circular No. 847 of 2020, as amended by CBE Circular No. 8 of 2021 and subsequent November 2022 directives on FX liquidity, all Egyptian exporters, including IoT hardware retailers selling cross-border, must repatriate 100% of export proceeds to an onshore foreign-currency account at a CBE-licensed Egyptian bank within 90 days from the date of shipment (bill-of-lading date). The exporter is then required to convert 100% of the repatriated proceeds to Egyptian pounds through the banking system unless the CBE has granted an exceptional retention waiver. Compliance is evidenced through submission of the customs export manifest, the CBE Form No. 304 export-settlement declaration, and the underlying purchase order/FX invoice. Failure to comply triggers bank-level suspension of further outward remittance facilities and referral to the CBE's Exchange Control enforcement unit.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: LOW FEASIBILITY as a primary treasury rail. Offshore electronic-money institutions (EMIs) such as Wise, Payoneer, Mercury, or Airwallex are neither licensed nor recognized by the CBE as eligible payment-service providers for Egyptian-resident corporate entities under Law No. 18 of 2019 (Payment Systems Law) and its executive regulations. An Egyptian LLC may only use such EMIs as auxiliary pay-in conduits for foreign e-commerce consumer card collections, provided that all funds are ultimately swept into an onshore CBE-licensed bank account within the 90-day export repatriation window and are accompanied by full merchant-level reconciliation. Establishing the EMI account in the name of the Egyptian LLC requires the EMI to comply with Egyptian residency rules, which virtually all offshore EMIs refuse to do; consequently, the company must not design its liquidity architecture around an offshore EMI balance.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence of at least one director is mandatory for LLC account opening at all major Egyptian banks. CBE AML/CFT Law (Law No. 80 of 2002, as amended) and the Unified Banking Law require the bank to conduct an in-person KYC interview with the client's authorized signatories and ultimate beneficial owners (UBOs) before activation. Remote onboarding is not generally available for a newly formed Egyptian LLC; a notarized power-of-attorney permitting a single director or agent to attend is acceptable in most banks, but the bank will still require the original passports, commercial registry extract, tax card, and proof of registered office. For entities with foreign shareholders not physically present in Egypt, the foreign shareholder must first appear before the Egyptian consulate in the shareholder's jurisdiction to execute the corporate resolutions and signature mandates, then the local director must attend the bank interview in Egypt.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident shareholder structure: the compliance officer questions the ultimate parent's source of funds and the economic substance of the Egyptian LLC.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: UAE/Egypt corporate chart, notarised and apostilled shareholder register, beneficial-ownership declaration under CBE Form BO-1, audited financial statements of the parent for the last two years, bank reference letters from the parent's home jurisdiction, source-of-wealth statement signed by each UBO, and proof of the Egyptian LLC's physical office lease.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Capital-injection ambiguity: the bank flags an inbound SWIFT categorized as a shareholder loan rather than a capital contribution.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarised shareholders' resolution approving the funding instrument, a formal loan or equity subscription agreement, the CBE Form No. 300 declaration (direct investment purpose code), the CBE no-objection letter on the capital schedule, and an ETA tax-registration certificate confirming the capital base.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: E-commerce revenue provenance: the bank questions the source of cross-border card proceeds from multiple international marketplaces and payment gateways.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Merchant settlement statements from payment processors (Stripe, Shopify Payments), marketplace sales reports, a sample of customer invoices and shipping tickets, the PCI DSS compliance certificate of each processor, and a written commissioned AML risk assessment confirming the entity's standard low-risk retail tier.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk jurisdiction routing: transactions or settlement flows pass through third-party payment aggregators domiciled in FATF-monitored jurisdictions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: The aggregator's regulatory licence in its home jurisdiction, a downstream KYC file on the aggregator, a detailed funds-flow diagram showing direct settlement to the Egyptian bank account, and a signed warranty from the aggregator that no prohibited end-user or sanctioned party is involved.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: All inbound capital injections, whether equity or shareholder loans, must be routed solely through a CBE-licensed Egyptian bank via SWIFT MT103 wire transfer quoting CBE purpose code 300 (direct investment in the capital of an Egyptian company) or code 302 (shareholder loan). The funds must be sourced from the shareholder's own bank account, not from a third-party aggregator, and must be accompanied by the notarised board resolution approving the injection, the company's incorporation contract (تيرخ), the ETA tax card, and a CBE Form No. 29 declaration filed by the bank's compliance unit within one business day of receipt. Proceeds for a capital increase must first be placed in a dedicated Capital Escrow Account and may only be utilized after the CBE issues its no-objection confirmation and the company completes the registration of the capital increase with the Commercial Registry. The bank will conduct a source-of-funds verification against the UBO's bank statements and may require a period of 5–10 business days for full settling of the remittance before crediting it to the operational account.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade settlements for IoT hardware imports are cleared via two primary rails: (i) direct SWIFT MT103 telegraphic transfers for invoices below the bank's low-value threshold (typically USD 50,000 per invoice), supported by a supplier proforma invoice, a CBE-issued import registration certificate (IRC), and preliminary customs declaration form; and (ii) irrevocable sight commercial letters of credit (UCP 600) for larger amounts, opened through the corporate bank against a proforma and a generated LC, with payment released against a clean on-board bill of lading, commercial invoice, packing list, and certificate of origin. Importers must appear on the CBE's registered importer list and all outward remittances must be covered by the company's CBE-approved annual FX budget as recorded in the bank's forward cover system. For fast-moving consumer IoT goods, the MT103 rail is preferred for speed, while the LC rail is reserved for high-value or recurring supplier relationships where the supplier requires payment assurance and the entity receives a 30–60 day usance.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore EGP/USD commercial forwards (FX forward contracts against verified trade documents, tenor up to 180 days, must be collateralized by a genuine import/export invoice)
Offshore EGP non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) executed by the parent entity outside Egypt to hedge EGP depreciation risk on repatriated dividends or shareholder distributions
Onshore currency swaps with a CBE-licensed bank for restructuring existing FX-denominated liabilities into EGP-denominated facilities, subject to CBE counterparty approval

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return (Income Tax Law No. 91/2005)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA), Ministry of Finance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 4 months after the fiscal year end; 30 April for calendar-year taxpayers (an alternate fiscal year requires prior ETA approval)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing surcharge of 25% of the assessed tax; delay interest accrues at 2% per month on the unpaid tax; willful evasion triggers fines of up to 200% of evaded tax and imprisonment.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual General Assembly Approval and Deposit of Audited Financial Statements with the Investment Regulator
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI), Companies Registration Division
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual general assembly must approve the financial statements and audit report within 6 months of the fiscal year end (by 30 June for calendar-year taxpayers); certified copies of the approved statements must be lodged with GAFI within 30 days of approval
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines of EGP 10,000–50,000 on managers for failure to lodge accounts; civil liability for misleading accounts; repeated non-filing gives GAFI authority to commence administrative strike-off proceedings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Commercial Register Renewal and Data Update
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commercial Register Office (General Department of Commercial Registration) via the GAFI one-stop shop
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Calendar-year renewal window from 1 to 31 January of each year; any change of managers, registered address, activities, or quota-holding structure must additionally be filed within 15 days of the event
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Monthly late-renewal fines; unregistered entities lose capacity to enforce trade contracts; prolonged non-renewal can result in administrative deregistration of the commercial registry record.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: National Social Insurance Annual Payroll Wage Statement and Contribution Reconciliation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Organization for Social Insurance (NOSI), Egyptian Social Insurance Authority
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Consolidated payroll wage statement for the prior calendar year filed in January of each year alongside the January monthly contribution declaration; all monthly declarations are due by the monthly filing deadline applicable to the employer's registration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: 2% monthly default surcharge on unpaid social contributions; criminal liability for deliberate evasion and false wage statements under Social Insurance Law No. 148/2019.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No size-based exemption: every Egyptian LLC, including single-shareholder and dormant LLCs, must appoint at least one licensed external auditor and file an independent audit report annually under Companies Law No. 194/2020; an audit is compulsory regardless of turnover, assets, headcount, or absence of banking debt.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Egyptian Accounting Standards (EAS), substantially converged with IFRS and issued by the Egyptian Accounting Standards Board under Law No. 194/2020 and Income Tax Law No. 91/2005; SMEs below the applicable threshold may use the simplified EAS for SMEs; consolidated IFRS/EAS reporting applies to groups and regulated entities.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Beneficial owners (natural persons controlling 25% or more of the LLC or exercising de facto control) must be recorded in the statutory records and re-confirmed annually during the January commercial-registry renewal and in the annual financial statement filing to GAFI; any change in beneficial ownership must be reported within 30 days; no restriction applies to non-resident ownership, but each non-resident owner must be identified with passport and tax identification data.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 250–800 per annum (shared registered office or administrative agent in Greater Cairo; premium business-address packages above USD 1,200)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 1,500–4,000 per annum for a single-entity SME smart-home IoT retail LLC operating under Egyptian Accounting Standards.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 22.5% (Income Tax Law No. 91 of 2005 as amended by Law No. 26 of 2020; resident Egyptian LLCs are taxed on worldwide income at this flat rate).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No automatic CIT reduction for smart-home IoT retail. Effective rate reductions arise only upon qualification: (i) 50% deduction of invested capital for projects in approved new urban communities and investment zones under Investment Law No. 72 of 2017; (ii) full CIT exemption for up to 5 years, renewable, for licensed Suez Canal Economic Zone (SCZONE) free-zone projects under Law No. 83 of 2002; (iii) participation exemption for dividends received from Egyptian-resident corporate shareholders; (iv) accelerated depreciation and 30% initial allowance on new machinery and equipment; (v) export-linked incentives under the unified incentives laws. Absent a special-zone license, the effective rate equals the 22.5% headline rate.
